jp: 友達[ともだち]に、おいしいラーメン屋[や]を教[おし]え{てもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: I had a friend tell me about a good ramen shop.
why: I am the receiver and the helper is marked with に, which fits てもらう.

jp: 店員[てんいん]さんに、プレゼントをきれいに包[つつ]ん{でもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: I had the shop assistant wrap the present nicely.
why: The assistant is marked with に and I benefit, so でもらう (after ん).

jp: 財布[さいふ]を忘[わす]れたので、友達[ともだち]に千円[せんえん]貸[か]し{てもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: I forgot my wallet, so I had a friend lend me a thousand yen.
why: I am the one lent to, with the lender marked by に, so てもらう.

jp: 子供[こども]の頃[ころ]、母[はは]に新[あたら]しいかばんを買[か]っ{てもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: When I was a child, my mother bought me a new bag.
why: With 母に marking the person who acts for me, the receiving pattern てもらう is used.

jp: 魚屋[さかなや]さんに、魚[さかな]を三枚[さんまい]におろし{てもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: I had the fishmonger fillet the fish for me.
why: I asked and received the service, with the fishmonger as に, so てもらう.

jp: 店[みせ]の人[ひと]に、商品[しょうひん]を箱[はこ]に入[い]れ{てもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: I had the shop staff put the goods into a box.
why: The staff are marked with に and I receive the service, so てもらう.

jp: 値段[ねだん]が高[たか]いので、店員[てんいん]さんにもう少[すこ]し安[やす]くし{てもらいたいです|gv-temorau}。
en: The price is high, so I would like the clerk to lower it a little.
why: I want the clerk (に) to do something for me, so てもらいたい.

jp: 会計[かいけい]のとき、友達[ともだち]にお金[かね]を払[はら]っ{てもらいました|gv-temorau}。
en: At the register, I had my friend pay for me.
why: The friend is marked with に and pays on my behalf, so てもらう.
